_note: Merged 2026-10-10 from Jerry's and quantrungvu's drafts (Claude). Jerry reviews. id = the mistake 'tag' used by the AI, stats and coach (quantrungvu's names kept; change an id only together with tests/sentences.json). rule = plain-English explanation the AI builds its short_explanation from. severity: 'major' = wrong meaning or core grammar (word goes back to box 1); 'minor' = accents, small spelling, punctuation. wrong/right = the main example; examples = all of Jerry's examples. focus_pos = kinds of target words that are good practice for the rule (coach's 'Practise this' button). Keep a rule with id 'other'.

rules.title: Le/la, un/une (gender)
rules.rule: Every French noun is masculine or feminine. Use le / un for masculine and la / une for feminine.

rules.title: Missing article
rules.rule: In French a noun almost always needs a small word in front of it, like le, une or des.

rules.title: Du, de la, des (some)
rules.rule: For an amount of something you can't count, like bread or water, use du, de la or de l'.
rules.wrong: Je bois l'eau tous les jours.

wrong: Je bois l'eau tous les jours.

rules.title: Au, aux, du, des
rules.rule: à le always becomes au, and à les becomes aux. de le becomes du, and de les becomes des.

rules.title: J', l', d' before a vowel
rules.rule: Before a vowel or a silent h, short words drop their last vowel: je becomes j', le and la become l', and de, ne and que become d', n' and qu'.

rules.title: Être (to be)
rules.rule: être goes: je suis, tu es, il/elle/on est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont.

rules.title: Avoir (to have) and age
rules.rule: avoir goes: j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.

rules.title: -er verbs in the present
rules.rule: For -er verbs, remove -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

rules.title: Irregular verbs in the present
rules.rule: Some very common verbs don't follow the normal pattern and have to be learned, like je vais, je fais, je prends, je veux, je peux.

rules.title: Verb matches the subject
rules.rule: The verb ending must match who is doing the action (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils).

rules.title: Adjective matches the noun
rules.rule: An adjective changes to match its noun: add -e for feminine and -s for plural.

rules.title: Where the adjective goes
rules.rule: Most adjectives go after the noun. A few short common ones (grand, petit, bon, beau, jeune, vieux, nouveau) go before it.

rules.title: Ne … pas
rules.rule: Put ne before the verb and pas after it. ne becomes n' before a vowel. (In casual speech people drop ne, but in writing keep it.)
rules.wrong: Je mange pas ne de viande.
rules.right: Je ne mange pas de viande.

wrong: Je mange pas ne de viande.
Il ne aime pas le froid.
right: Je ne mange pas de viande.

rules.title: Asking questions
rules.rule: Ask with est-ce que + normal sentence, or a normal sentence ending in '?'. Question words go first: Où est-ce que..., or at the end in casual speech: Tu vas où ?

rules.title: À, en, au + places
rules.rule: Use à for cities, en for feminine countries, au for masculine countries, dans for 'inside', chez for 'at someone's place'.

rules.title: Mon, ma, mes
rules.rule: mon, ma and mes match the thing you own, not the owner. Use mon before a feminine word that starts with a vowel (mon amie).

rules.title: Word order
rules.rule: A normal French sentence goes subject + verb + the rest, like in English.
rules.wrong: Le matin bois je un café.
rules.right: Le matin, je bois un café.

wrong: Le matin bois je un café.
right: Le matin, je bois un café.
Je bois un café le matin.

rules.title: Fixed prepositions
rules.rule: Some verbs and expressions always take the same preposition: avoir besoin de, penser à, jouer au (sport) / du (instrument).

rules.title: Aller + infinitive (near future)
rules.rule: To say what you're going to do, use aller in the present + the basic form of the verb: je vais manger.

rules.title: Avoir or être in the past
rules.rule: Most verbs use avoir in the past (j'ai mangé). Movement verbs like aller, venir, partir, arriver, and reflexive verbs, use être (je suis allé).

rules.title: Past participle form
rules.rule: The past form of -er verbs ends in -é (mangé). Many common verbs are irregular: fait, pris, vu, bu, eu, été, dit, écrit, lu, mis.

rules.title: Object pronouns (le, la, lui, en, y)
rules.rule: Object pronouns go before the verb: je le mange, j'y vais, j'en veux.

rules.title: Imparfait or passé composé
rules.rule: Use the imparfait for background and habits in the past (il faisait beau), and the passé composé for a finished action (je suis sorti).
rules.wrong: Quand j'étais petit, j'ai joué au foot tous les jours.
rules.right: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au foot tous les jours.

rules.title: Comparing (plus, moins, aussi … que)
rules.rule: Compare with plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que. Bon becomes meilleur.
rules.wrong: Ce café est plus bon que l'autre.
rules.right: Ce café est meilleur que l'autre.

rules.title: Qui or que
rules.rule: Use qui when the next word is a verb (the person who does), que when a new subject follows (the thing that I see).
rules.wrong: Le livre qui je lis est bon.
rules.right: Le livre que je lis est bon.

rules.title: Si + imparfait, conditionnel
rules.rule: For an imagined situation: si + imparfait, then the conditional: si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.
rules.wrong: Si j'aurais le temps, je voyagerais.
rules.right: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.

rules.title: Subjunctive after il faut que
rules.rule: After il faut que, je veux que, pour que and similar, use the subjunctive: il faut que je parte.

rules.title: Word choice
rules.rule: The word you used means something else in French, or is an English word written in a French way.

wrong: Je vais à la librairie pour emprunter un livre.
right: Je vais à la bibliothèque pour emprunter un livre.

rules.title: Spelling and accents
rules.rule: A missing or wrong accent, or a small typo, that doesn't change which word it is.

rules.title: Capitals and punctuation
rules.rule: Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop, or with '?' for a question. French puts a space before ? ! : ;.

rules.title: un / une / du / des become de after a negative
rules.rule: After ne ... pas, un, une, du, de la and des change to de (or d').

wrong: Il ne boit pas de l'eau.

rules.title: avoir for age, hunger, thirst, cold...
rules.rule: French uses avoir (to have), not être, for age, hunger, thirst, being cold or hot, and being afraid.

rules.title: Words about yourself match your own gender
rules.rule: When you talk about yourself, adjectives and past forms with être match you: a woman writes je suis fatiguée and je suis allée, a man writes je suis fatigué and je suis allé.

rules.title: Choosing the right question word
rules.rule: où = where, quand = when, combien = how much / how many, pourquoi = why, comment = how, qui = who, quoi / qu'est-ce que = what.

wrong: Quand tu pars ? (when you meant why)

rules.title: il y a (there is / there are)
rules.rule: 'There is' and 'there are' are both il y a. It never changes for plural.
rules.wrong: Il y ont des chats dans le jardin.
rules.right: Il y a des chats dans le jardin.

wrong: Il y ont des chats dans le jardin.
right: Il y a des chats dans le jardin.
Il n'y a pas de pain.

rules.title: Time expressions (le lundi, à 8 heures, en juin)
rules.rule: Use à for clock time, en for months and years, and le + day for 'every Monday'. Use no word at all for 'this Monday'.

rules.title: Second verb stays in the infinitive (aimer, vouloir, pouvoir + infinitive)
rules.rule: When two verbs follow each other, only the first changes. The second stays in its basic form (manger, aller).

rules.title: Passé composé with être: agreement
rules.rule: With être, the past form matches the subject: add -e for a woman and -s for plural.

rules.title: devoir / pouvoir / vouloir / avoir envie de
rules.rule: je dois = I must, je peux = I can, je veux = I want, j'ai envie de = I feel like. The next verb stays in its basic form.

rules.title: Reflexive verbs (se lever, s'appeler)
rules.rule: Verbs with 'se' (se lever, s'habiller) are actions you do to yourself: 'lever' is to lift, 'se lever' is to lift yourself, so to get up. 'se' changes with the person: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons. In the past they use être: je me suis levé(e).
rules.right: Je me lève à sept heures.

right: Je me lève à sept heures.

rules.title: Linking ideas: mais, et, donc, parce que, quand
rules.rule: mais = but, donc = so, parce que = because, quand = when. parce que becomes parce qu' before a vowel.
rules.wrong: Je reste ici parce que il pleut.
rules.right: Je reste ici parce qu'il pleut.

wrong: Je reste ici parce que il pleut.
Il est fatigué, mais il dort. (when you meant 'so')
right: Je reste ici parce qu'il pleut.
Il est fatigué, donc il dort.

rules.title: quel / quelle / quels / quelles
rules.rule: quel (which / what) matches its noun: quel for masculine, quelle for feminine, and add -s for plural.

rules.title: Other mistakes
rules.rule: Use only when no other tag fits. Jerry reviews these to decide whether to add a new rule.
